BY THE OPTIMIST DAILY EDITORIAL TEAM

Nine months in, North America’s largest wildlife overpass has cut vehicle collisions on a stretch of Interstate 25 in Colorado by 91 percent. Before it opened, that corridor was averaging roughly one deer hit per day during peak migration.

The crossing, a 209-by-200-foot structure near the Greenland exit between Larkspur and Monument, opened in December. It came in ahead of schedule and under budget. Five underpasses and miles of fencing channel animals toward the safe crossings.

Like ugly bookends, two first-inning touchdowns summed up the Rockies’ main issue this season. 
In Colorado’s home opener on April 3, the Phillies blasted Michael Lorenzen for seven runs in the opening frame. And in the Coors Field finale on Sept. 24, the Diamondbacks obliterated Tanner Gordon for six runs in the first. In both games, the Rockies were down 8-0 after two innings as neither the veteran Lorenzen nor the young Gordon could stop the bleeding.
Those two performances encapsulated Colorado’s starting pitching problem, which has long been the central riddle for the Rockies to solve. The enigma has been exacerbated amid the Rockies’ recent nadir, as the club has endured four straight seasons with 100-plus losses.
